span: reservation of posts in promotion is dependent on the inadequacy of representation of members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes
why: Reports the holding of Suraj Bhan Meena (reservation in promotion depends on quantifiable data) as part of a survey; this passage does not itself adopt it.

span: provision of Article 16(4A) is an enabling provision and State is not bound to make reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the matters of promotion
why: Court restates the Constitution Bench: the State may provide reservation in promotion but must collect quantifiable data and respect limits; the permission is conditional.

span: continued social backwardness of the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes employees has necessarily to be assessed
why: Counsel's submission about reading Article 16(4-A) to require assessing continued backwardness; a party argument whose direction on the proposition is not clear.

span: sub-classification of backward and more backward classes would be permissible
why: Indra Sawhney discussion on sub-classifying backward classes; not reservation in promotion.

span: promoted in accordance with the policy of reservation in promotion provided for in the Reservation Order
why: Quoted section of a State Act protecting consequential seniority; it presupposes reservation in promotion but is statute text, not the court's holding.

span: it was necessary to continue the existing dispensation by providing reservation in promotions
why: Court describes why Art. 16(4-A) was added (Statement of Objects and Reasons); it narrates the amendment's purpose rather than stating a holding.
